title: CRLR/327/2022 of AMIT KACHWAHA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 327 of 2022
Amit Kachwaha ....Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Another ..... Respondents
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for the private respondent.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to
the order of interim maintenance dated 02.05.2022,
passed in Case No. 111 of 2019, Smt. Saumya Saini Vs.
Amit Kachwaha, by the court of Family Judge, Haridwar
("the case"). By it, an application for interim
maintenance, filed by the private respondent, the wife,
has been allowed and the revisionist has been directed
to pay Rs.50,000/- per month as interim maintenance to
the private respondent.
2. Heard learned counsel for the revisionist
and perused the record.
3. The revisionist and the private respondent
were married on 25.01.2015. There was a matrimonial
discord and they both started staying separate. The

2
private respondent filed an application under Section
125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, read with
Section 7 (f) of the Family Courts Act, 1984, based on
which the proceedings of the case instituted. In the case,
the application for interim maintenance was filed, which
has been allowed by the impugned order. It is impugned
herein.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the impugned order is not in accordance
with law. It warrants interference. He made the following
submissions in his arguments:-
 (i) The affidavit, which was
required to be filed by the private
respondent pursuant to the
judgment in the case of Rajnesh Vs.
Neha and Another (2021) 2 SCC
324, is not complete. It does not
reveal various things. The
respondent no.2 did not give her
bank account details. Fixed Deposit
Receipts ("FDR") have not been
disclosed in the affidavit.
 (ii) If the private respondent is
unwell, she could get the money for

3
her treatment through the
insurance policy, which has been
taken by the revisionist even for the
private respondent. But, it has not
been considered in the impugned
order.
 (iii) The revisionist did not
conceal anything in the case. He
disclosed every detail of his account
deposits, etc. The revisionist filed
an application in the court below
stating therein that the private
respondent had concealed the
details of bank accounts and FDR,
but no order was passed on such
application. For the want of such
documents with regard to income,
etc. of the private respondent, the
court could not have been in a
position to arrive at a just
conclusion.
5. It is also argued that, in fact, the private
respondent is a qualified Dentist. She treats patients
even today and holds camps. This factor has not been

4
taken into consideration; the private respondent is not
unwell because she is still pursuing admission for Post-Graduation. Certain documents have been referred to.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the
private respondent would submit that the revisionist
cannot claim that for the want of complete information,
filed pursuant to the judgment in the case of Rajnesh
(supra), the impugned order has been vitiated. It is
argued that, in fact, in his affidavit filed pursuant to the
judgment in the case of Rajnesh (supra), such details
have not been given by the revisionist; he has not
disclosed is income tax returns for the years, as required
under Heading F sub-clause 7 of the affidavit; bank
statements were not filed. It is also argued that if the
revisionist is trying to obtain higher education, it may
not be termed bad; the revisionist concealed his present
income; he has a huge income; he has also opened a
firm in Canada, but in a criminal proceeding, he has
been restrained to go abroad. Therefore, no interference
is warranted.
7. During the course of argument, on behalf
of the revisionist, reference has been made to certain
parts of the judgment in the case of Rajnesh (supra) to

5
argue that the purpose of affidavit is, in fact, to assist
the court.
8. In the case of Rajnesh (supra), the Hon'ble
Supreme Court, inter alia, observed that, " It is often
seen that both parties submit scanty material, do
not disclose the correct details, and suppress vital
information, which makes it difficult for the Family
Courts to make an objective assessment for grant of
interim maintenance." Further, the Hon'ble Supreme
Court also observed that, "The objective of granting
interim/permanent alimony is to ensure that the
dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or
vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage,
and not as a punishment to the other spouse. "
9. It is a revision against the order granting
interim maintenance. Much of the discussion is not
expected of. It is true that the affidavits filed pursuant to
the judgment in the case of Rajnesh (supra) filed by the
parties in the court below do not contain complete
details, specifically, under caption F. There are 9 sub-heads, but both the parties have consolidated it in 7
sub-heads. In fact, in the affidavit filed by the
revisionist, the income tax details have not been

6
enclosed. Simply in sub-heading 5, the answer is given
that the revisionist files income tax returns. Its effect
would definitely be considered by the court below if such
issue is raised before the court or when it comes to the
notice of the court. The affidavit, itself, at the bottom,
gives a declaration by the deponent that he would be
liable to punishment under the criminal law if such
provisions are attracted.
10. The factum of FDR and different bank
accounts by the private respondent is admitted. There
have been explanation to it. The Court refrains to go in
those controversies.
11. Reference has been made on behalf of the
revisionist that the private respondent is a qualified
dentist and she attends patients. Definitely, the purpose
of maintenance is to give support to a wife, who is
somehow staying separate from her husband and is
unable to maintain herself. It depends on various
incidents, including the status of the parties, financial
resources, qualification and other attending factors.
Even if the private respondent is attending some
patients, merely on that basis it cannot be said that she
is able to maintain herself. Even if the private

7
respondent is pursuing for post graduation, at this
stage, it cannot be said that she is not unwell. In fact,
during the course of hearing, the Court explored the
possibility of amicable settlement between the parties. At
that stage, the revisionist admitted that his wife has
some ailment for which, in fact, according to the
revisionist, he quit his job and stayed with his wife for a
long.
12. In the impugned order, the monthly salary
of the revisionist has been assessed as Rs. 1,87,430/-,
based on the income tax returns. It is argued on behalf
of the revisionist that he has to maintain his father and
a sister. It is his responsibility. Even keeping in view
that responsibility, the amount of interim maintenance,
as has been awarded, cannot be said to be excessive.
13. Having considered the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that the court below did not commit
any error. This Court does not see any reason to make
any interference and the revision deserves to be
dismissed.
14. The revision is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 30.09.2022
